decision: Do not promote this adapter; retain base NuExtract3 as proposal extractor with source review. This small pilot does not establish that fine-tuning is generally unhelpful.

qualitative_review.finding: Adapter recovers the fork identity and XRT 2.20-header/2.25-runtime compatibility observation that the base omitted. Both still phrase third-party physical results as facts without explicit reported/hearsay wording in the statement or conditions.

Base emits a README-tested NPU driver version as an unqualified run fact and calls the commit date a run date despite the source saying the run date was not stated. Adapter removes those metadata assertions but omits the four numeric rate observations and generates a non-verbatim condition: prompt grows from 1k to 8k tokens.
Both omit the Q4_K_M and Q8_0 prompt-rate comparisons and their reported gains. Adapter combines multiple assertions into fewer records; fewer records do not establish better atomicity.
Adapter retains the /dev/dxg path that the base statement omitted, but combines GPU passthrough, absent NPU execution/timing and host-only availability into one record.

metric_limits: Citation validity is mechanical, not semantic support.
The exact qualifier diagnostic requires entire reference headlines in generated statements/conditions and is too strict to interpret as scope accuracy here.
Quote-overlap counts can match a wrong or compound statement and are not semantic recall.
Nine training passages, one validation passage and four fixed test passages are a bounded pilot, not a broad capability estimate.
All held-out references and review decisions are agent-authored; no independent human adjudication or upstream-log verification.
metadata_correction: Original generated outputs and original summaries remain in *.initial.* files; reference provenance wording was corrected after inference. Future evaluation code records the annotation provenance directly.
